raw_response:
Hey. Let me think this through. I've been working this land for 45 years now, and at 65 I'm not as quick as I used to be. It's just me and the old lady at home — the kids are working in the city, send money back when they can. Sixteen mu is a lot for two old people, so I have to be smart about what goes where, and I hire the combine for wheat harvest and pay for some help when the cotton needs picking.

Let me think about each piece of land...

The biggest piece, about 10 mu of the flat land near the well, that's my wheat-maize ground. Same as always. Plant wheat in October after Hanlu, harvest in June, then turn around fast and put maize in the same week. That's how everyone here does it. My neighbor old Liu and I, we've been doing this rotation for 30 years.

For wheat, I buy a bag of compound fertilizer (15-15-15) before planting, that's about one bag per 1.5 mu, and then when the wheat starts jointing in spring I topdress with urea, maybe half a bag per mu. That's what works. Some years if money is tight I cut back a little. The extension fellow said one time I should put 18 kg of nitrogen but I just go by bags, my way works fine. Yield is usually around 400 kg/mu, sometimes 450 in a good year.

For maize after the wheat, I use the hybrid seed, the Zhengdan or whatever the agro-shop is selling that year. Hybrid seed is expensive — 50 yuan a mu — but everyone uses it now, the local seed doesn't yield. I put down urea when planting and again at big trumpet stage. Two irrigations usually, three if the summer is dry. I get maybe 450 kg/mu.

Then I have about 3 mu of cotton on the sandier piece on the west side. Cotton is hard work for old people — all that picking by hand, three or four times in the fall. I hire two women from the village to help pick, pay them by the day. I keep doing cotton because the price has been decent and that piece of land doesn't grow wheat well. Plant late April, fertilize at planting and again at squaring, spray for bollworm a couple times.

The other small pieces — peanut, millet, mung bean — those are mostly for the family. Peanut on 1.5 mu, the soil is good for it, doesn't need much fertilizer because it's a legume. Millet on about 1 mu, that's drought-tolerant, I plant it on the corner that's hard to irrigate. Mung bean on 0.6 mu, just for our own table and to give some to the kids when they visit. These small crops I don't put much money into.

Total cash for inputs this year, I'm figuring around 4,500 yuan. That's about all I can spend. If anything breaks or the well needs repair, that comes first.
